iwgdf.basis: No loss of protective sensation and no PAD

report.headline: Urgent review recommended
report.patient_summary: The scan shows features strongly associated with diabetic foot ulceration. Please contact a podiatrist, diabetes foot clinic or urgent care service today. Keep weight off the foot and do not attempt to treat the area yourself.
report.clinical_assessment: Automated analysis returns a fused ulceration risk of 95.0% (HIGH). The convolutional classifier assigned P(ulcer) = 99.3% to the plantar image (temperature-calibrated, T = 1.00); clinical covariates applied a +0.00 log-odds adjustment. No clinical covariates were supplied, so the reported risk reflects image evidence alone. IWGDF stratification places this patient in category 0 (Low risk) on the basis of: no loss of protective sensation and no pad.
report.visual_analysis: Grad-CAM++ attribution for the ulcer class shows 2 discrete regions of activation together covering 33.9% of the field, with the dominant focus upper-left. Peak activation 1.00, mean 0.37, spatial focality 0.66 (1.0 = single tight hotspot). The classifier assigned P(ulcer) = 0.993 to this image.
report.triage:
1. Same-day or next-working-day podiatry / foot-clinic review
2. Vascular assessment: palpate pedal pulses, measure ankle-brachial index
3. Neurological assessment: 10 g monofilament at ten plantar sites
4. Probe-to-bone test; image and screen for osteomyelitis if positive
5. Institute pressure offloading (total contact cast or removable walker)
6. Wound swab and empirical antibiotics only if clinical infection is present
7. IWGDF risk category 0 (Low risk) - recommended screening interval: Annually

report.limitations: Single-image analysis of a cropped plantar patch. The model was trained on 224x224 tissue patches and has not been validated on whole-foot photographs, on skin tones outside the training distribution, or against histopathology. Clinical coefficients are literature-informed priors, not fitted to outcomes in this cohort. Wound depth, infection and ischaemia are not assessed.
